evidence.quote: Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring.
Thus, only one satellite is required.
The proposed satellite would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM) for research and/or education.

criteria.reasoning: Mission purpose, Australian benefit, single-spacecraft rationale and likely users are described in detail with references. Operator is only implied (Australian facilities/government), and user/funding roles are somewhat vague, so low Accomplished.

evidence.quote: The proposed satellite will thus use the Vega E rocket as a launch vehicle – launched from the Guiana Space Centre Spaceport.
The most suitable orbit for this task would be a low-earth sun-synchronous orbit.
Systems Tool Kit 11 (STK) was used to calculate access periods as seen below:
The most promising alternative is a ‘drag sail’

criteria.reasoning: All major design areas are covered with STK screenshots and an access table, but support is incomplete: no STK files, no quantitative swath/resolution, launch performance, link budget or drag-lifetime calculations. Launch selection is speculative and some orbit/EOL claims are inconsistent.

evidence.quote: A specific launch vehicle – the Vega E – has been selected although it has not been built yet.
The Mt Pleasant Radio Observatory is well-located to receive data from this orbit type constantly and for long durations.

criteria.reasoning: Conclusions restate the main design choices and are linked to the body, but they are brief and partly generic. The claim of constant ground-station contact is inaccurate, and EOL conclusions are omitted.

Report structure and headings are clear, but presentation is not professional: figures/tables lack numbers and captions, references are URL-only and mismatched, Wikipedia is used, and several typos/contradictory statements remain.

technical_issues.issue: Launch choice relies on a 2021 VV18 example and the unbuilt Vega E; no performance/azimuth analysis for direct injection from 5.05°N into a 97.8° retrograde SSO, and Wikipedia is used as the launch database.
The statement that high altitude yields low resolution images “which is also desirable” is contradictory; the 600 km altitude is not derived from required swath, resolution or sensor field of view.
RAAN is stated to indicate launch-facility location; RAAN depends on launch time/azimuth and orbital dynamics, not facility latitude alone. J2 precession rate is stated but not calculated.

Mount Pleasant Radio Observatory is a radio-astronomy facility, not an established EO downlink station; no link budget, data rate or data-volume assessment supports the claim that passes are sufficient. Access results cover only three days.

Five-year life is asserted without component/lifetime analysis. Drag-sail EOL is proposed without drag area, deployment reliability, orbital-lifetime, 25-year-rule or casualty-risk calculation; no propulsive manoeuvre is actually designed.
References in tables [49]-[55] and [66]-[74] are absent from the bibliography; bibliography entries are bare URLs and include Wikipedia.

overall: A readable preliminary design that addresses all mission areas with STK evidence, but it is weakened by missing software files, unquantified trade-offs, an unbuilt launch vehicle, inaccurate/contradictory statements and poor referencing. Adequate overall.
